dedupe_keys.name: predictive and prescriptive models for diesel fuel supply chain operations in hurricane relief duque yang and morton preprint 2020

description: This record describes predictive and prescriptive models for diesel fuel supply chain operations in hurricane disaster relief, presented in a May 2020 preprint by researchers at Northwestern University and Los Alamos National Laboratory. The authors build a model that estimates diesel fuel demand from historical weather forecasts and power outage data, and feed it into a stochastic programming model run in a rolling-horizon fashion to dispatch tank trucks as a hurricane approaches and passes. They describe the result as a data-driven optimisation tool for decision support and report numerical results on the key aspects of operations. Coverage is the US Atlantic and Gulf coast context named in the introduction. Access: the preprint is a free PDF on Optimization Online; no software or data release and no licence are stated on the pages read, so the models are documented but not offered as a package. Caveats: only the abstract and introduction were read, and the data sources and validation are described in the full text. It suits optimisation and resilience studies of fuel supply during storms, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
